title: Parallel Lines and Transversals Core Test
description: Identify angle relationships created by parallel lines and transversals, then use them to solve for unknown angles.

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle is 72 degrees. Its corresponding angle measures what?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel.

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle is 64 degrees. Its alternate interior angle measures what?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal for parallel lines.

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle is 53 degrees. Its alternate exterior angle measures what?
questions.explanation: Alternate exterior angles are equal for parallel lines.

questions.questionText: Two same-side interior angles are formed by parallel lines and a transversal. One is 118 degrees. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary: 180 - 118 = 62.

questions.questionText: A linear pair includes one angle of 47 degrees. What is the other angle?
questions.explanation: A linear pair adds to 180 degrees.

questions.questionText: Vertical angles are formed at an intersection. One angle is 109 degrees. What is the vertical angle?
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are equal.

questions.questionText: Which angle pair is equal when two parallel lines are cut by a transversal?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles match in position and are equal.

questions.questionText: Which angle pair adds to 180 degrees when the lines are parallel?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary.

questions.questionText: A transversal crosses two lines. What extra fact lets you use corresponding angles as equal?
options: The two crossed lines are parallel.
The diagram is drawn on graph paper.
questions.correctAnswer: The two crossed lines are parallel.
questions.explanation: Corresponding angle equality depends on parallel lines.

questions.questionText: An angle is 84 degrees. The angle adjacent to it on a straight line is what?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles on a straight line form a linear pair.

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Angle A and angle B are corresponding. If angle A = 3x + 8 and angle B = 68, what is x?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal, so 3x + 8 = 68 and x = 20.

questions.questionText: Alternate interior angles are labeled 5x - 10 and 85 degrees. What is x?
questions.explanation: Set 5x - 10 = 85, so 5x = 95 and x = 19.

questions.questionText: Same-side interior angles measure x + 44 and 101 degrees. What is x?
A corresponding angle is 124 degrees. What is the same-side interior angle paired with it on the same side of the transversal?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary: 180 - 124 = 56.

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle of 38 degrees has a vertical angle at the same intersection. What is that vertical angle?
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are equal.

questions.questionText: An alternate exterior angle is 117 degrees. What is the corresponding angle to that alternate exterior angle?
questions.explanation: Both relationships preserve equality in this parallel-line diagram.

questions.questionText: Which statement is always true for parallel lines cut by a transversal?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal; same-side interior and linear pairs are supplementary.

questions.questionText: Angle 1 and angle 2 are same-side interior angles. Angle 1 is 7x and angle 2 is 5x. What is x?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles add to 180: 7x + 5x = 180.

questions.questionText: A pair of alternate interior angles measures 4x + 11 and 2x + 53. What is x?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal: 4x + 11 = 2x + 53.

questions.questionText: A pair of corresponding angles measures 6x - 5 and 4x + 31. What is x?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal: 6x - 5 = 4x + 31.

questions.questionText: Same-side interior angles measure 2x + 20 and 3x + 35. What is x?
questions.explanation: Their sum is 180: 5x + 55 = 180.

questions.questionText: A transversal forms a 143 degree angle with one parallel line. Which angle pair must measure 37 degrees?
options: A vertical angle to the 143 degree angle
An alternate interior angle to the 143 degree angle
A linear pair with the 143 degree angle
A corresponding angle to the 143 degree angle
questions.correctAnswer: A linear pair with the 143 degree angle
questions.explanation: A linear pair is supplementary: 180 - 143 = 37.

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Angle A is 69 degrees. Angle B is alternate interior to angle A. Angle C forms a linear pair with B. What is angle C?
Which evidence is enough to conclude two lines are parallel?
options: A pair of adjacent angles add to 180 at one intersection.
A pair of alternate interior angles are equal.
Two angles in the same triangle add to 90.
questions.correctAnswer: A pair of alternate interior angles are equal.
questions.explanation: The converse of the alternate interior angle relationship can prove lines parallel.

questions.questionText: A pair of same-side interior angles are 80 degrees and 100 degrees. What can you conclude?
options: The lines may be parallel because the angles are supplementary.
The transversal is not a line.
questions.correctAnswer: The lines may be parallel because the angles are supplementary.
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles that add to 180 support parallel lines.

questions.questionText: Two corresponding angles measure 2x + 14 and 5x - 40. If the lines are parallel, what is x?
questions.explanation: Set the corresponding angles equal: 2x + 14 = 5x - 40.

questions.questionText: An exterior angle and its alternate exterior partner are labeled 8x - 7 and 5x + 29. What is x?
questions.explanation: Alternate exterior angles are equal: 8x - 7 = 5x + 29.

questions.questionText: If one angle in a parallel-line transversal diagram is 121 degrees, what are the measures that appear in the diagram?
questions.explanation: Equal and supplementary relationships create only the angle and its supplement.

questions.questionText: An angle is supplementary to 73 degrees and corresponding to angle M. What is angle M?
questions.explanation: The supplement is 107, and corresponding angles are equal.

questions.questionText: A same-side interior pair is 4x + 2 and 6x - 12. What is x?
questions.explanation: They add to 180: 10x - 10 = 180.

questions.questionText: Which angle pair is inside the parallel lines and on opposite sides of the transversal?
questions.explanation: Inside plus opposite sides describes alternate interior angles.

questions.questionText: Which angle pair is outside the parallel lines and on opposite sides of the transversal?
questions.explanation: Outside plus opposite sides describes alternate exterior angles.

questions.questionText: A corresponding angle pair is 88 degrees and 88 degrees. What must be true if those angles came from two lines and a transversal?
options: The equal corresponding angles are evidence the two lines are parallel.
The lines must intersect at 88 degrees.
The angles form a linear pair.
questions.correctAnswer: The equal corresponding angles are evidence the two lines are parallel.
questions.explanation: Equal corresponding angles can prove lines parallel.

questions.questionText: A same-side interior pair is 93 degrees and 87 degrees. What is their relationship?
Two alternate interior angles are 3x + 6 and 75 degrees. What is x?
A diagram has parallel lines cut by a transversal. Angle A corresponds to angle B, and angle B forms a linear pair with angle C. If angle A is 42 degrees, what is angle C?
questions.explanation: B = 42 by corresponding angles, so C = 180 - 42.

questions.questionText: Same-side interior angles are labeled 3x + 15 and 7x - 5. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles add to 180: 10x + 10 = 180, so x = 17. The angles are 66 degrees and 114 degrees, so the larger angle is 114 degrees.

questions.questionText: Alternate exterior angles measure 9x - 4 and 6x + 35. What is each angle?
questions.explanation: Set 9x - 4 = 6x + 35, so x = 13 and each angle is 113.

questions.questionText: A student says alternate interior angles are supplementary. Which counterexample uses parallel lines?
options: A 70 degree angle and a linear-pair partner add to 180.
A 70 degree angle and a same-side interior partner add to 180.
A 70 degree angle and a 20 degree angle are complementary.
A 70 degree angle and its alternate interior partner are both 70 degrees.
questions.correctAnswer: A 70 degree angle and its alternate interior partner are both 70 degrees.
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal, not supplementary.

questions.questionText: Two lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of same-side interior angles measure 2x + 30 and 4x - 12. If x = 27, what can you conclude?
options: The lines are parallel because the angles are equal.
The lines are parallel because the same-side interior angles add to 180.
The lines are not parallel because one angle is obtuse.
No conclusion is possible because same-side interior angles never matter.
questions.correctAnswer: The lines are parallel because the same-side interior angles add to 180.
questions.explanation: The angles are 84 and 96, and 84 + 96 = 180.

questions.questionText: Angle A is alternate interior to angle B. Angle B corresponds to angle C. If angle C is 128 degrees, what is angle A?
questions.explanation: Corresponding and alternate interior relationships are equal relationships.

questions.questionText: A pair of corresponding angles are labeled 4x + 7 and 8x - 49. What is the supplement of either angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal, so x = 14 and each corresponding angle is 63 degrees. The supplement is 180 - 63 = 117 degrees.

questions.questionText: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. One angle is 35 degrees. Which statement describes the whole diagram?
options: Four angles measure 70 degrees and four measure 110 degrees.
Four angles measure 35 degrees and four angles measure 145 degrees.
Only one angle measure can be known.
questions.correctAnswer: Four angles measure 35 degrees and four angles measure 145 degrees.
questions.explanation: Vertical, corresponding, and alternate angle relationships create four equal acute angles and four supplements.

questions.questionText: A same-side interior pair measures 11x - 2 and 6x + 12. What is the smaller angle?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles add to 180: 17x + 10 = 180, so x = 10. The angles are 108 degrees and 72 degrees, so the smaller angle is 72 degrees.

questions.questionText: A pair of angles are equal, outside the parallel lines, and on opposite sides of the transversal. What are they?
questions.explanation: Outside and opposite sides describes alternate exterior angles.

questions.questionText: A proof says: angle 1 equals angle 2 because they are same-side interior angles. What should be corrected?
options: Same-side interior angles are never used with parallel lines.
Same-side interior angles are always vertical.
Same-side interior angles are supplementary, not equal.
questions.correctAnswer: Same-side interior angles are supplementary, not equal.
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles add to 180 degrees.

questions.questionText: If angle 1 and angle 2 are alternate interior angles, and angle 2 and angle 3 are a linear pair, which relationship connects angle 1 and angle 3?
questions.explanation: Angle 1 equals angle 2, and angle 2 plus angle 3 is 180.

questions.questionText: Two corresponding angles are 5x + 20 and 9x - 36. What is the angle measure?
questions.explanation: 5x + 20 = 9x - 36 gives x = 14, so the angle is 90.

questions.questionText: A pair of same-side interior angles are 12x + 4 and 5x + 6. What is x?
questions.explanation: They add to 180: 17x + 10 = 180.

questions.questionText: A student concludes two lines are parallel because a pair of alternate interior angles are 64 degrees and 66 degrees. What is the issue?
options: Alternate interior angles must add to 180.
The angles are not equal, so that evidence does not prove the lines are parallel.
The angles are too small to use.
Only corresponding angles can prove lines parallel.
questions.correctAnswer: The angles are not equal, so that evidence does not prove the lines are parallel.
questions.explanation: Equal alternate interior angles can prove parallel lines; nearly equal is not enough.
